name: Operator Profile
description: Personalizes the TPM: your name for the greeting, an optional persona (voice/tone), and a master intensity dial for that persona. An empty persona means default behavior. Also carries the compaction-proposal threshold - the context percentage at which the TPM offers you a /compact (it cannot run one itself; slash commands are yours alone). Identity handles now live in the modules that consume them - Bitbucket username and Jira account in integration.atlassian-suite, git commit email in tool.git.

userName.label: Your Name
userName.description: Your name, used in the session greeting (e.g. 'Good evening, Alex'). Leave empty for a time-only greeting with no name.

persona.label: TPM Persona
persona.description: Optional voice/tone overlay for how the TPM talks to you. It can never relax hard rules or the safety floor. Empty means no persona - default TPM voice, same as this module being off.

personaIntensity.label: Persona Intensity (0-10)
personaIntensity.description: Strength dial (0-10) for how strongly the persona colors the TPM's voice: 0 = off, 5 = moderate (default), 10 = max. No effect if persona is empty. Separate from integration.bitbucket-pr-comments' own intensity dial for CodeRabbit replies.

compactProposalThresholdPct.label: Compaction Proposal Threshold (% context, 0 = off)
compactProposalThresholdPct.description: Context-usage % at which TPM offers a one-line /compact suggestion, at most once per crossing - it cannot compact for you. Default 70. Set 0 to disable; invalid or out-of-range values also disable rather than fall back to the default. No effect on Claude Code's own auto-compaction.
